## Purpose and entry points
Mindcraft is a Node.js multi-agent Minecraft automation framework: LLM-backed Mineflayer bots perceive a Minecraft world, converse, plan, and execute embodied actions. `main.js` is the CLI entry point; global connection/runtime settings originate in `settings.js`, while selected agent behavior and model configuration comes from profile JSON such as `andy.json` and `profiles/*.json`.

## Process startup and agent lifecycle
Startup parses CLI settings/profiles and creates isolated agent processes. The process boundary is implemented by `src/process/init_agent.js` and `src/process/agent_process.js`. Each worker constructs an agent, connects its Minecraft client, and coordinates shutdown/reconnection through `src/agent/connection_handler.js`. This separation supports multiple configured agents in one run.

## Core agent orchestration
`src/agent/agent.js` is the behavioral hub: it combines conversation input, world state, prompt/model responses, skills, memory, and action execution. `src/agent/conversation.js` manages interaction turns and agent-to-agent/player communication; `src/agent/history.js` retains conversational context. `src/agent/modes.js` controls operating modes, including constrained behavior versus LLM-directed operation.

## Action, skills, and world boundary
The agent’s only embodiment boundary is the Mineflayer/Minecraft runtime. `src/agent/action_manager.js` schedules and monitors actions, while `src/agent/commands/actions.js` and `src/agent/commands/queries.js` expose operational and observation commands to the agent. Reusable Minecraft capabilities and state gathering live in `src/agent/library/skills.js`, `src/agent/library/skill_library.js`, and `src/agent/library/full_state.js`. Patched Mineflayer ecosystem dependencies in `patches/` are material compatibility/runtime extensions.

## LLM, code, and memory pipeline
Model calls are selected through `src/models/_model_map.js` and provider adapters such as `src/models/gpt.js`, `src/models/claude.js`, and `src/models/ollama.js`; providers can be cloud APIs or local endpoints. `src/models/prompter.js` constructs model-facing requests. `src/agent/memory_bank.js` and `src/utils/examples.js` support retained/retrieved context and example selection, with embeddings when the configured provider supports them. `src/agent/coder.js` enables model-authored actions; it is a security-critical boundary because generated code may execute, though coding is disabled by default.

## Perception and communication extensions
Minecraft chat output and optional speech synthesis pass through `src/agent/speak.js`. Vision is optional and separated into capture, viewer integration, and interpretation: `src/agent/vision/camera.js`, `src/agent/vision/browser_viewer.js`, and `src/agent/vision/vision_interpreter.js`. `src/agent/mindserver_proxy.js` connects agents to the companion server/control plane when used.

## Server, UI, and deployment
The companion Mindcraft server is implemented by `src/mindcraft/mindcraft.js`, `src/mindcraft/mindserver.js`, and `src/mindcraft/mcserver.js`; static UI assets are under `src/mindcraft/public/`. Deployment supports local Node execution or Docker via `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`. Bots connect to a local LAN or remote Minecraft Java server; remote authentication may use Microsoft accounts. For unsupported protocol versions, `services/viaproxy/` provides an optional proxy path.

## Task/evaluation execution
CLI task mode injects goals, inventories, constraints, and timeouts into agents for repeatable single- or multi-agent episodes. Runtime task logic is in `src/agent/tasks/tasks.js`, `src/agent/tasks/crafting_tasks.js`, and `src/agent/tasks/construction_tasks.js`; task datasets and batch/evaluation scripts are under `tasks/`. Construction NPC goals and blueprints are represented by `src/agent/npc/controller.js`, `src/agent/npc/build_goal.js`, and `src/agent/npc/construction/`.
